story: In this illustrative pruning path, larger alpha selects fewer leaves. Several smaller candidates preserve the same best held-out accuracy; choose the smallest on that plateau before accuracy drops.

aha.observation: Alpha 0.01 gives six leaves at the best held-out accuracy of 90%. Larger alpha shrinks further but loses accuracy in this series.

data.title: Prune until accuracy begins to drop.
data.heading: Illustrative pruning path
data.prompt: how does cost-complexity pruning trade tree size against accuracy as alpha increases?
data.instructions: Increase alpha through the supplied settings. Find the smallest tree still on the best-accuracy plateau.
calculations: The supplied leaf-share series is percent of 10 initial leaves. Leaf count = share/100 × 10.
Choose maximal supplied held-out accuracy, then minimal leaf count among tied candidates: 90%, 6 leaves, alpha 0.01.
Removed leaves = 10 − selected leaves. Retained share = selected leaves/10 ×100.
No fitted topology or training-risk values were supplied. The count strip represents counts only; no numeric R_train + alpha*leaves objective or actual pruned branches are invented.
data.sourceKind: illustrative path; unrelated to the eight-row toy topology
